description: Transcription (invariant 16, single application of a bridge): the narrow scope premise (if Jesus holds a mandate from g and founded the Catholic Church as a visible society with authority, he founded it in that mandate and commissioned it to teach) follows from the report-to-event premise for the reported commissions (Matthew 28.18-20 and at least one of Matthew 16.18-19, 18.17-18, John 20.21-23, 21.15-17 go back to Jesus) and the premise that a governing power and the power to teach, if Jesus gave them, make his founding of the Catholic Church a founding in the mandate with a teaching commission. The proof takes the power to teach from Matthew 28's reported powers and, by cases on the four governing reports, a governing power, and applies the second premise to them. The second premise has the conclusion's two parts as consequents and is strictly weaker than the conclusion; the derivation is content-sensitive (in a preaching-only model it fails, and both premises are needed by omission models), but the 'institution or message' question is relocated, not decided: it now lies in the historical premise. It verifies consequence only: both premises remain open. The institutional conclusions are taken directly from the consequents of STMT-CHURCH-FOUNDED-IN-COMMISSIONED-APOSTLES; the case analysis on the reported powers only supplies its antecedents, and the omission countermodels do not change that. So the result derives no institutional content and, by the closure rule, leaves the narrow premise open while either premise is open.
